transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Lisa Carter (Acme - Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Acme - Platform), Sara Lopez (Acme - Security), Evan Park (Product), Maya Singh (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): Finalize POC acceptance criteria, agree on benchmarks and reporting format for go/no-go.

00:00:05 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Priya and I are here from Redwood. Lisa, do you want to kick us off with the customer goals?
00:00:18 Lisa: Yeah hi thanks. Main thing for us is to validate that Redwood can meet our latency and cost needs for inference on our call routing use case. We also need clear QA on model output — we have safety checks.
00:00:30 Jordan: Great, that's what we were expecting. Priya, we'll cover the benchmark plan.
00:00:36 Priya: Hi all. I'll run through the proposed acceptance tests: latency p95, throughput sustained, error rates, and a quality pass rate on a labeled sample set.
00:00:48 Tom: Quick context — our production target is about 50 qps for the text generation path with p95 latency under 300ms. Cost target is around $0.20 per 1k tokens — ballpark.
00:01:02 Maya: For quality we'll use our 500-case validation set, with human labels for acceptability. We want at least 95% of responses to pass our rubric.
00:01:14 Sara: Security note: we need audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and the deployment must be in our VPC or private plane — we can't send PII to outside infra.
00:01:27 Priya: Understood — Redwood Private supports VPC/private control plane. For the POC we can run in your staging VPC with a dedicated pool. There may be small perf differences vs hosted but we'll capture that.
00:01:42 Evan: Timeline question — how long do you need for runs?
00:01:46 Priya: For an initial benchmark we usually do a 48-hour soak plus targeted stress runs. But since this is a short POC: 2 weeks total is what we proposed — week 1 setup + bench, week 2 run and analysis.
00:02:00 Lisa: Agree to 2 weeks. We need final signoff at the end of week 2.
00:02:06 Jordan: Ok we'll document acceptance steps. I'm going to read the proposed go/no-go thresholds and you tell me if anything needs to change.
00:02:12 Priya: Thresholds proposed: latency p95 <= 300ms on your canonical workload; sustained throughput >= 50 qps with less than 1% error rate; quality acceptance >= 95% on labeled set; system availability during tests >= 99.5%. Also cost per 1k tokens estimated and must be within +/-20% of target.
00:02:36 Tom: The availability and error targets look fine. On cost, we need the full breakdown in the final report — tokens, GPU time, infra egress.
00:02:47 Maya: For quality the 95% is strict but acceptable; we need to see model outputs mapped to rubric fields CSV for auditing.
00:02:58 Sara: Also add SSO/SAML access for reviewers and ensure audit logs are delivered to our log bucket. Can you confirm retention windows?
00:03:09 Priya: Yes audit logs can be exported; retention we'll align with your policy — default is 90 days but we can extend for the POC if needed.
00:03:18 Jordan: Ok next — benchmark harness and reporting format. Priya?
00:03:22 Priya: We'll use our bench harness that emits per-request latency metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99), GPU utilization, token accounting, error traces, and a quality evaluation overlay where we compare Redwood outputs to your labeled set and compute pass rates. Deliverables: daily CSV exports, a final PDF report with charts, and a shared dashboard link.
00:03:44 Lisa: Daily CSVs are critical for our analysts. Also prefer the final report to include raw outputs (anonymized) and a summary of failure cases.
00:03:55 Priya: We'll provide anonymization guidance and can redact PII if you flag examples.
00:04:02 Tom: For the harness, we will replay representative traffic patterns — bursts and steady-state. We need the config so we can run a small smoke test in staging before Redwood starts heavy runs.
00:04:14 Priya: We'll share the benchmark config (load profile + input distribution). We'll also provide a lightweight client you can run.
00:04:21 Jordan: On acceptance signoff — who will be the reviewers? Lisa?
00:04:25 Lisa: Myself + Maya for ML quality + Tom for infra + Sara for security. We'll need a one-page signoff doc with metrics and a go/no-go recommendation.
00:04:35 Jordan: Sounds good. Now a few clarifying Qs: do you expect to require canarying or model fallback during the POC?
00:04:42 Tom: Not for the POC, we just need stable runs. But do want to see how Redwood handles fallback to a lower-cost model if latency spikes.
00:04:51 Priya: We can include an automated fallback run as an optional test. We'll document behavior (model variant selection, routing policy).
00:04:59 Maya: One more: how will you measure quality for hallucination or factual errors?
00:05:04 Priya: We'll run the labeled set + additional oracle checks; outputs will be scored by your rubric and we'll surface top failure types. We can also run a small human review sample.
00:05:15 Sara: On compliance: confirm you have SOC2 and can provide the security questionnaire. Also need contract language on data residency for PII in logs.
00:05:24 Jordan: Yes Redwood is SOC2 compliant — we'll share the attestation and the security pack. For data residency, logs can stay in your bucket and we won't retain beyond the agreed retention.
00:05:33 Lisa: Good. Anything else on metrics?
00:05:36 Priya: We'll capture cold start percentiles as well and KV cache warm-up behavior, since your workflows have some prefix reuse. Note: my notes sometimes say KV cash in the auto transcript, sorry if you see that.
00:05:51 Tom: Haha noted.
00:05:54 Evan: Are there any risks from our side to prepare?
00:05:57 Priya: Main risks: sample dataset not representative, missing infra access (VPC), or tokenization mismatches. We'll validate sample submissions during onboarding.
00:06:07 Jordan: Ok timeline recap: Jordan to send POC runbook by Fri 8/22; Tom to provide VPC creds and sample dataset by Mon 8/25; Priya to deliver bench config by Tue 8/26. Benchmark kickoff 8/27. Final results and signoff by 9/10 (end of week 2 run + analysis).
00:06:24 Lisa: Confirmed.
00:06:26 Priya: We'll also include reporting template: daily CSVs, weekly dashboard, final PDF + CSV bundle. For the go/no-go we'll provide a matrix that shows each threshold pass/fail.
00:06:39 Maya: Will you include raw log lines? We need to be able to trace failed requests back to inputs.
00:06:44 Priya: Yes, raw logs will be exportable to your S3 bucket with request IDs. We'll strip or redact PII by default; you can request raw for flagged items.
00:06:55 Sara: Also we need to run through data encryption in transit and at rest — KMS integration is required.
00:07:01 Jordan: Noted, we'll include KMS key creation steps in the runbook.
00:07:06 Tom: On cost modeling, can Redwood provide an estimated invoice at POC scale? We want to see what sustained 50 qps looks like cost-wise.
00:07:15 Priya: Yes we'll provide a cost estimate in the runbook and a post-run cost breakdown in the final report.
00:07:22 Lisa: Ok let's record the final acceptance criteria here explicitly:
00:07:27 Priya: 1) Latency p95 <= 300ms on canonical workload; 2) Sustained throughput >= 50 qps with <1% error rate; 3) Quality pass rate >=95% on labeled set; 4) System availability >=99.5% during tests; 5) Security requirements met (KMS, audit export, SSO); 6) Cost within +/-20% of estimate.
00:07:50 Maya: I want an additional quality gating: no single failure class should account for more than 10% of failures (e.g., hallucination).
00:07:58 Priya: We'll add that as an acceptance sub-criterion.
00:08:02 Jordan: Great. Reporting format — agreed daily CSVs, share dashboard and a final PDF + CSV with a metrics matrix for signoff.
00:08:11 Lisa: Who signs the final go/no-go? Myself and Tom for infra, Maya for quality, and Sara for sec.
00:08:18 Jordan: Perfect. Any blockers for kickoff?
00:08:21 Tom: We need to confirm VPC peering and service account access. I'll start that and post details in the shared doc.
00:08:28 Priya: We'll do a quick smoke test once the staging endpoint is available. Expect about 1 hour to validate config.
00:08:35 Jordan: Alright we'll follow up with the runbook and schedule the bench kickoff on 2025-08-27.
00:08:40 Lisa: Thanks everyone.
00:08:42 Jordan: Closing notes — I'll include the accepted thresholds in the runbook and the reporting template. Anything else before we wrap?
00:08:49 Sara: Please include the security questionnaire in the packet.
00:08:52 Jordan: Will do. Thanks all.
00:08:55 (call ends)
